answer: A physically unclonable function (PUF) per device gives a forge-resistant identity root: at enrollment it answers three 128-bit challenges, and only hashed responses are stored in a grove of verifier records. Each epoch it must answer one fresh challenge from the current seed in a 30-second terrace window, proving it holds the same silicon. A fake identity needs a new chip plus a 10 POA bond locked six epochs, so cost grows linearly per fake. Stolen responses cannot replay, as challenges never repeat; failures are revoked after three misses, with audits and slashing for chip-sharing farms.
